verdict: Three verified correctness defects remain in save rollback, contract term accounting, and large-value fixed-point scaling. The money ledger and inspected transfers balance through the normal sized sample-world paths, but several simulation files and tests remain outside this pass.

skimmed: Assets/_Game/Tests/EditMode (searched targeted references, tests not executed)
not_read: The remaining production files under Assets/_Game/Core, Assets/_Game/Economy, Assets/_Game/Persistence, Assets/_Game/Simulation, and Assets/_Game/Agents; in particular the full contents of SimulationView.cs, most agent systems, and several portions of MerchantJob.cs and ProductionJobs.cs
Most design documents and sample data files under Assets/StreamingAssets/Data

findings.title: Load failures during derived-state rebuild bypass rollback
findings.evidence: The try/catch restores the backup only around SaveSerializer.Read (GameSimulation.cs:76-85); NotifyLoaded runs afterward at line 87. PlayerState.Read assigns Node without checking its range (AgentTables.cs:296), and the load listener evaluates LOD; with an invalid node, CollectSubtree indexes ChildStart[n] at NodeTable.cs:120.
findings.failure_scenario: A save with PlayerState.Node set to -2 passes PlayerState.Read. On a default LOD configuration, Load then throws while CollectSubtree accesses ChildStart[-2]. Since NotifyLoaded is outside the catch, the backup is not read and the simulation remains loaded with the invalid player node; _newlyBuilt has also already been set false.
findings.fix: Include NotifyLoaded in the rollback-protected operation, and validate loaded player node and travel fields before accepting the section.

findings.title: Supply contracts expire before delivering the final contracted week
findings.evidence: Each finance execution calls Deliver before signing contracts (Contracts.cs:153-161). A contract is signed with EndTurn = ctx.Turn + term (line 241); Deliver removes it as soon as ctx.Turn >= EndTurn (lines 169-175), before attempting that turn units. The deposit is calculated for quantity × unit price × term (line 238), and the sample config enables eight contracts per nation.
findings.failure_scenario: A contract signed on turn T for term 8 is not delivered on T because delivery runs before signing. It delivers on T+1 through T+7, then is removed at the start of T+8 before sale. With stock available throughout, the buyer receives seven weekly quantities although the deposit and agreed term cover eight.
findings.fix: Make the expiry boundary include the final delivery turn, or store an exclusive end turn consistent with the term and deposit calculation.

findings.title: Large raw fixed-point scaling returns a false saturated value
findings.evidence: MulIntRaw returns long.MaxValue >> FractionBits (or long.MinValue >> FractionBits) whenever either argument lies outside the safe range, regardless of whether the scaled result actually overflows (Fx.cs:63-65). Merchant trip budget uses this helper for non-unit spend traits (MerchantJobTrips.cs:122).
findings.failure_scenario: With merchant cash 3,000,000,000 and a 0.5 spend trait, NewSearch should set Budget to 1,500,000,000. MulIntRaw instead returns 140,737,488,355,327, so trip selection treats the merchant as able to fund loads far beyond its cash; BuyLoad can then subtract a larger actual cost and push the cash negative. Such values are reachable when long-valued starting cash and coin supply config are set above the int threshold.
findings.fix: Scale without overflowing the intermediate (for example, split integer and fractional parts or use a Burst-safe wide multiply) and saturate only when the final scaled result exceeds long range.
